title: Encouragement of Economic Independence in Islam
summary: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ emphasized self-reliance and the virtue of lawful earning.
translation: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) encouraged commerce after migrating from Mecca to Medina by establishing a market for Muslims there. The emigrants typically engaged in trade while the locals focused on agriculture. The Prophet reformed their economic efforts, emphasized the virtue of commerce, and encouraged craftsmen, small-scale workers, and farmers. Women whose husbands were unable to work would sell homemade goods in the market as a source of income. They asked the Prophet if spending on their husbands and children was rewarded; he affirmed it was. The Prophet praised all efforts in animal husbandry and agriculture in the pursuit of lawful income. Economic self-sufficiency reduces dependency, as seen when residents of Medina, once indebted to Jewish moneylenders, became prosperous through diligent work. He highlighted self-reliance with an example of a young, healthy man working hard, noting that efforts to avoid dependency are rewarded by God and are in God's way. Thus, striving for lawful earnings is commendable.
